# pengdows.efcore.adonet

> A reusable ADO.NET core that EF Core 10 relational providers build on. The core holds the shared EF Core-to-ADO.NET implementation; each database is added as a dialect plugin that describes and implements what makes it different. Any database with an ADO.NET driver can be added as a plugin, and the EF Core provider for it is the core plus that plugin.

## Project purpose

- Implement common EF Core query and update, mapping, command, connection, transaction, migrations, and provider infrastructure once, in the core.
- Keep database syntax, type mappings, capabilities, and custom EF services in independently maintained dialect plugins.
- The core never names a database. Adding one must not require changing it; if it does, that is a missing extension point.
- Plugins compile against the packed core with no `InternalsVisibleTo`; `docs/PUBLIC_API.md` lists the extension points.
- Cross-test the design across SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, DuckDB, and the flat file. The flat file is the ISO SQL baseline.

## Migrations and locking

- A database's migrations take a lock that matches how it can be shared:
  - a server database uses a session lock (`sp_getapplock` on SQL Server, `GET_LOCK` on MySQL);
  - a file- or directory-based database takes an exclusive sidecar lock file (`<database>.migrations.lock`), which the operating system releases when the holder exits;
  - a single-writer database (one writer at a time, any number of readers) must have such a lock file, and a single-writer dialect with none to name refuses to migrate.
- The lock coordinates migrations only. The library does not control writers during normal use; that is pengdows.crud's job.

## Testing without a database

- The EF Core core and dialect code can be exercised with `pengdows.crud.fakeDb`, a standalone in-process ADO.NET provider used as test infrastructure. It covers LINQ translation, SQL and parameter generation, command execution, reader materialization, change tracking, SaveChanges, transactions, async flows, and injected failures.
- `pengdows.crud.fakeDb` is a test-only dependency; the runtime packages do not reference it.
- Real database tests are still needed for engine semantics, query execution, migrations, and type fidelity. Some tests use embedded SQLite instead of fakeDb.

## Databases not supported

- Google Cloud Spanner's native ADO.NET provider (`Google.Cloud.Spanner.Data`) does not satisfy the ADO.NET contract that pengdows.crud and pengdows.efcore.adonet require, as the conformance tests show. Support will be reconsidered when the defects are corrected and verified. Spanner remains supported in pengdows.crud through Npgsql and PGAdapter, using its PostgreSQL interface.

## Relationship to pengdows.crud

`pengdows.efcore.adonet` is a separate project from [pengdows.crud](https://github.com/pengdows/pengdows.crud). Like EF Core in general, it does not have what makes pengdows.crud different: connection governance (`PoolGovernor`, reader and writer pools, pool protection, reserves, adaptive gates, fairness, backpressure), intent-based routing and read-only enforcement, execution modes (`Standard`, `PreventDatabaseUnload`, `SingleWriter`, `SingleConnection`), tenant database orchestration, the SQL-first `ISqlContainer` and `TableGateway` APIs, `RetryContext`, adaptive load control, and pengdows-specific metrics. Those will not be integrated here: pengdows.crud is a different architecture, and porting them to EF Core would mean rearchitecting EF Core.

What this project takes from pengdows.crud:

- `pengdows.crud.fakeDb`, for the database-free tests above.
- `pengdows.stormgate.EntityFrameworkCore`, for optional pool protection: a limit on concurrently open EF Core connections with fail-fast backpressure. It is injected and configured separately; the provider contains no `PoolGovernor` or admission policy.

Standard EF Core logging, diagnostics and framework metrics remain available. Normal ADO.NET driver pooling is not pengdows.crud pool governance.

## Entry points

- [README](https://github.com/pengdows/pengdows.efcore.adonet/blob/main/README.md): purpose, architecture, plugin contract, supported engines, testing.
- [Source-level code review](https://github.com/pengdows/pengdows.efcore.adonet/blob/main/docs/CODE_REVIEW.md): findings, remediation status, open items.
- [Public API rationale](https://github.com/pengdows/pengdows.efcore.adonet/blob/main/docs/PUBLIC_API.md): exported contracts, extension points, and documentation debt.
- [Performance measurements](https://github.com/pengdows/pengdows.efcore.adonet/blob/main/docs/PERFORMANCE.md): the measurements behind the performance findings.
- [Review policy](https://github.com/pengdows/pengdows.efcore.adonet/blob/main/REVIEW_POLICY.md): rules for PR reviews.
- [pengdows.crud](https://github.com/pengdows/pengdows.crud): the SQL-first data-access library with governance, routing, tenancy and operational capabilities.
